meta.description: Full-stack developer from Amsterdam. Backends with Node.js, Express and FastAPI, frontends with React, Next.js and Angular, with an interest in AI and cloud.

hero.title: I build software from database to interface.
hero.intro: Full-stack developer from Amsterdam with an Associate Degree in Software Development. Backends with Node.js, Express and FastAPI, frontends with React, Next.js and Angular. I am most interested in AI and cloud.

nimbus.subtitle: AI customer service as SaaS
nimbus.text: SaaS platform that lets companies deploy an AI chatbot to answer customer questions. From documentation and design to implementation and tests.

alt.phone: Mobile view of the Nimbus dashboard

captions: Desktop dashboard, designed in Figma and built to match it exactly
built: Product vision, requirements, roadmap and complete project documentation: architecture, API design, database design and security
A custom design system and every screen in Figma, for desktop, tablet and mobile
A backend with FastAPI and PostgreSQL (with pgvector), with database migrations in Alembic
An AI chatbot that answers questions from a company's knowledge base, using the Claude API
Tests at three levels (unit, integration and end-to-end) with Pytest and Vitest, and CI/CD with GitHub Actions
nimbus.role: Everything, from idea and design to code and tests. A personal project to show that I can design, document and build a complete SaaS product.

pipeline.subtitle: Local RAG with OCR
pipeline.text: Local RAG pipeline that reads scanned inspection reports with OCR, summarizes them and makes them searchable, with source references. Built for Your Data Company.

alt.summary: Summary of an elevator inspection report with the eight steps of the pipeline
alt.questions: Question about a report with an answer and page source
alt.ocr: Text extracted with OCR from a scanned report

captions: The eight steps of the pipeline on the left, the summary with findings, actions and source numbers on the right
A question about the report, answered with a reference to the page
A scanned report: the text was extracted from the image with OCR
The overview of processed reports, two of which were scanned and read with OCR
built: A pipeline in eight steps: validation, text extraction with OCR, chunking, embeddings, storage, retrieval, summarization and source validation
OCR with Tesseract (Dutch and English) for scanned reports
Summaries and answers with Gemma 3, running locally through Ollama, with no API key or usage costs
Asking questions about a report, with a page source for every answer
Tested with pytest, Ruff and mypy in the backend and ESLint and TypeScript in the frontend
pipeline.role: Assignment for a job shadowing day at Your Data Company: build a working proof of concept within a single day, from design to tested code.

pbn.title: PBN Inventory Management
pbn.subtitle: Graduation internship · mobile
pbn.text: Mobile app that lets employees report stock per location, with a QR scanner, product database, status overview and admin panel. Built from scratch by a team of two.

alt.home: Home screen of the PBN inventory app

built: Reporting stock per location and project, with quantities per product
A QR scanner to recognize products quickly, with manual search as an alternative
An overview of previous submissions and their status
A product database with standard packaging and a photo
An admin panel for products, users and roles, with JWT authentication in the backend
pbn.role: Ten-week graduation internship. Built from scratch together with one other developer: designed in Figma first, then frontend and backend. The handover is documented, so a successor can pick it up.

avennex.subtitle: Cloud · in development
avennex.text: Cloud platform on Azure that processes battery sensor data to detect fire risk early. As cloud engineer, I manage the infrastructure as code with Terraform.

alt.architecture: Cloud architecture of AvenNex Ember on Azure
alt.c4: C4 container diagram of the Ember DEV environment in Azure

captions: The cloud architecture at a glance
C4 container diagram, including management with Terraform
built: A sensor (ESP32) sends measurements over MQTT/TLS to Azure IoT Hub
A Function App processes new measurements every minute and stores them in PostgreSQL
A Read API serves the data to the rider's app
Secrets are kept in Key Vault, with a managed identity for the Function App; logs and metrics go to Application Insights
The infrastructure is defined in Terraform, with a GitLab pipeline that formats, validates and scans every change
avennex.role: Cloud engineer in the team. I manage the Azure environment as code: terraform plan on every change, and deployment only after the client approves.

about.title: Who I am, beyond the code
paragraphs: I'm Ilias, I live in Amsterdam and I most enjoy working on software that people actually use. What I do at work really started on the football pitch.

When I was four, I first stepped onto the pitch at AVV Zeeburgia, and I kept playing until I was sixteen. What I learned there, I now see in every team: you win together, you speak up when something isn't right, and you show up even when it rains.

These days I train at the gym three to four times a week on a PPL split: push, pull and legs. Now and then I play padel with a friend, sometimes with four of us, just for fun. I like to read, from Harry Potter to the news, and in my spare time I experiment with local LLMs.
